audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Akshan six of seven stages while Sion wins 52.76% over 1666 games; the packet itself flags the contradiction. I did not change the chart because nothing in the kits or the mirror settles which stage should flip.
audit.why: Changing rows on a hunch would ship a false power shift, and level-chart edits are validated as an atomic group.
audit.corrected: Left the chart alone and raised it as a question. The stage prose was corrected instead: level 1 is chip, not an unanswerable double-shot, and the level 6 stage now names Comeuppance's missing-health scaling as the real reason not to brawl low.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes and whys described 'two E charges' and a level-6 spike built on a revive passive, with no cooldowns anywhere.
audit.why: Heroic Swing has no charges — it is one cast on 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s. Comeuppance is 100/85/70s and scales with the target's missing health, which is the actual level-6 spike.
audit.corrected: whys[1] now gives the 18s swing and Avengerang's 850 range; whys[4] names Comeuppance and its missing-health scaling; mid gives the 15s rank-3 swing cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text repeatedly claims Akshan pokes with a 'camouflage Q double-shot' off his E swing, and that his revive passive triggers when you kill him.
audit.why: Camouflage belongs to Going Rogue (W) and only engages while moving toward a Scoundrel — it is not a lane poke tool. The double shot is Dirty Fighting (P), the extra reduced-damage attack. And Going Rogue resurrects his allies when HE kills the Scoundrel who killed them, i.e. when he kills you after you took one of his teammates — not when you kill him.
audit.corrected: Every 'camouflage double-shot' line restated as Avengerang plus Dirty Fighting's extra attack; the revive wrinkle in late and wants.foe[2] restated in the correct direction. Also named Roar of the Slayer's armour shred and Soul Furnace's 3-second detonation per the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late field contains invented damage figures ('he pokes for 400, your W-shield absorbs 600') and a stray '}' at the end of the string.
audit.why: Neither number is derivable from the kits, and the brace is a data defect that renders on the page.
audit.corrected: Numbers removed, brace removed in the same edit.

edits.before: Akshan opens with camouflage Q double-shot from his E swing before your Q even charges — you have no answer at level 1 and take the poke.
edits.after: Akshan pokes with Avengerang out and back while Dirty Fighting adds a second shot — you have no answer at level 1 and take the chip.

edits.before: He has two E charges now and can lap around your charging Q twice; his poke damage outpaces your threat.
edits.after: Heroic Swing is up every 18s off any wall, and Avengerang out-ranges your charge at 850; his poke outpaces you.

edits.before: Your R gives a threat vector but his E lets him dodge the charge by swinging perpendicular; his revive passive punishes a sloppy all-in.
edits.after: Comeuppance stores bullets that scale with your missing health, and Heroic Swing angles him off your charge line; commit only with the stun.

edits.before: Swing in with E grapple, proc passive camouflage double-shot, and exit before your Q charges
edits.after: Swing in on Heroic Swing, land Dirty Fighting's extra shot, and exit before your Q charges

edits.before: Keep his revive passive live by tracking ally deaths and threatening to undo any kill you earn
edits.after: Mark you a Scoundrel by trading kills, then kill you to resurrect the ally you took down

edits.before: Akshan's E grapple lets him swing in, proc his passive camouflage Q double-shot, and disengage before your Q charges — you cannot punish him without a stun landing first.
edits.after: Heroic Swing anchors on any wall so he can swing in, land Avengerang and a Dirty Fighting shot, and leave before your Q charges — punish needs the stun first.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are Akshan's best window and he knows it. His E grapple lets him swing across a wall anchor, land a Q double-shot from camouflage, and be back behind minions before your Q even finishes charging. Do not stand still trying to full-charge Q — he reads the animation and disengages the instant your feet leave the ground. Use your W-shield proactively to absorb his poke rather than saving it for an all-in, because he will never let you all-in him at this stage. Farm and accept lane pressure; your passive means he gains nothing from trading kills.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are Akshan's best window and he knows it. Heroic Swing anchors on a wall, so he swings across, fires Avengerang plus a Dirty Fighting shot, and is back behind minions before your Q finishes charging. Do not stand still trying to full-charge Q — he reads the animation and disengages the instant your feet leave the ground. Use Soul Furnace proactively to absorb the poke rather than saving it for an all-in, because he will never let you all-in him at this stage. Farm and accept lane pressure; your passive means he gains nothing from trading kills.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay uncomfortable. He has enough E charges to lap around you and your Q is still a snail's telegraph on a mobile ranged target. At 6 your R gives you a threat vector — if he is standing far from a wall anchor your R can close the gap faster than his E exits — but he will respect this and hug terrain. Your best mid-game play is to bait a greedy E grapple onto a minion wave near you, flash or R the remaining gap, and land the charged Q. One knockup is a full trade won; he has no armor, no real defensive cooldown once his E is down, and your E armor-shred then W-detonate sequence will chunk him hard. Track his E charges before committing.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay uncomfortable. Heroic Swing is back every 15s at rank 3 and your Q is still a snail's telegraph on a mobile ranged target. At 6 your R gives you a threat vector — if he is standing far from a wall anchor your R can close the gap faster than his swing exits — but he will respect this and hug terrain. Your best mid-game play is to bait a greedy grapple onto the wave near you, flash or R the remaining gap, and land the charged Q. One knockup is a full trade won; he has no real defensive cooldown once the swing is down, and Roar of the Slayer's armour shred into a Soul Furnace detonation chunks him hard. Track that 15s before committing.

edits.after: This is why the matchup is FAVOURED for you despite the painful lane. At 2+ items your HP total is so large that his burst does not end trades — he chips, Soul Furnace eats the window, and your zombie passive threatens him even as you die. He cannot splitpush against you because your R covers 7500 units and one knockup in a side lane is a kill. Going Rogue runs the opposite way to how it reads: he resurrects a fallen ally by killing the Scoundrel who took them, so after you claim a kill, do not hand him yours. Force objectives after every skirmish you win, where the HP advantage is decisive and his mobility loses value.

notes: This matchup has no full-layer entry at all — all edits are content-layer. The late field on disk ends with a stray '}' which is removed by this edit. Every 'camouflage double-shot' claim was fabricated: camouflage is Going Rogue (W) and only runs toward Scoundrels; the extra shot is Dirty Fighting (P). The revive direction was also backwards and is corrected.
